attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: Narrowing 'its current work' to Imagen and LaMDA fits the immediate context. 'Refused' is slightly stronger than 'opted out', but it is close enough. The rhetoric about the trappings of science is left unscored.

contract.note: Reading 'community inspection' as meaningful external scientific access is fair and ordinary. Limiting the claim to the named models and to 2022 is reasonable. How to count exceptions under 'systematically' still affects the result.

evidence.note: Google's own disclosure says it chose not to release Imagen code or a public demo. This supports withholding for Imagen. The page is a live copy, not an archived Sept 2022 capture, and it says nothing about private researcher access.
Constrained LaMDA demos rolled out gradually to small consumer groups, with internal red-teaming. This neither shows independent scientific access nor documents that researchers were refused.

reviews.rationale: For Imagen, Google's own disclosure supports non-release. For LaMDA, the packet shows only constrained consumer demos. Neither item records whether outside researchers asked for or got access. The packet itself says there is no complete record for either model, so 'systematic' withholding across both is not established. Nothing contradicts it either.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words about his own view and his bet offer.

semantics.note: The proposition covers both his disagreement with Musk and the bet offer. Staking money on the outcome turns 'I think' into a firm commitment that AGI would not arrive by 2029. The 'unlikely' modality understates that, but the scoring direction is unchanged.

contract.note: Using the five tasks from the original bet offer is fair, since the offer is what he refers to. The contract rightly excludes the single-system rule added in June 2024. The deadline is the end of 2029.

evidence.note: Marcus's own 2022 offer setting out the five tasks and the three-task threshold. It defines the terms only. The speaker's own words cannot prove the outcome. It is mislabelled as a company disclosure.
A Sept 2026 review that finds the published evidence does not support claims that GPT-6 Astra is AGI. It does not test the five original tasks, so there is no conclusive event.

reviews.rationale: The deadline is 2029-12-31, after the evaluation date. No independently verified demonstration meeting three of the five original tasks is in the packet, so the early-resolution rule for contradiction is not met. Absence of success cannot support the forecast before the deadline, so it is not yet scored.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Faithfully states a universal negative about public demonstrations up to the post date, using a five-year-old as the benchmark.

contract.note: Reading the benchmark as robust sentence composition comparable to a typical five-year-old is ordinary. Requiring age-matched baselines is strict, but it applies equally to support and contradiction.

evidence.note: Winoground (April 2022) shows large gaps between models and humans. Its human baseline is adult crowdworkers, with no five-year-old comparison, so it is suggestive but not decisive.

reviews.rationale: The only evidence item compares models with adult crowdworkers, and models fall well short. There is no comparison with five-year-olds, and the packet has no survey wide enough to show that no qualifying demonstration existed by Sept 2022. Nothing contradicts the claim. The available evidence does not settle it.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps the core claim that current systems are weak on compositionality and that compositionality is central to language. The 'most linguists' wording and the 'bloviating' rhetoric are reasonably not scored as a headcount.

contract.note: The plain reading, that prominent contemporary neural systems had substantial compositional weaknesses but not that every architecture fails, is fair and ordinary. The 2022 window matches the context.

evidence.note: Winoground (April 2022): models across all attention types struggled compared with humans, mostly scoring near chance on composition-dependent matching.
COGS comparison (Feb 2022): seq2seq models, including BART, score very low on structural generalization. Specialized compositional parsers do well, which qualifies the claim but does not undo it.
A 2020 paper stating compositionality as a defining property of language. Background for the linguistics point only, not 2022 outcome evidence.

reviews.rationale: Two 2022 studies show substantial compositional failures in prominent neural model families. One covers vision-language models on Winoground; the other covers seq2seq models, including BART, on structural generalization. The specialized parsers that succeed are narrow exceptions, not the 'current systems' said to have mastered language. Linguistic research treats compositionality as central.
